articles.title: Happy Children's Day 2026: Top 50 Wishes, Messages and Quotes to share with your loved ones
articles.summary: Every year on November 14, India sets aside a day to celebrate childhood.
articles.body: Every year on November 14, India sets aside a day to celebrate childhood. In 2026 it falls on a Saturday, which means more time for family outings, school programmes and long, lazy afternoons with the kids. It’s the perfect excuse to tell the children in your life how much they matter.Sometimes the hardest part is finding the right words. So here are 50 wishes, messages and quotes you can send, write in a card, post as a status or say out loud. Pick the ones that sound like you, and feel free to tweak them with a nickname or an inside joke.Warm Wishes for ChildrenHappy Children’s Day! May your day be filled with giggles, sweets and all your favourite games.Happy Children’s Day, little one! Stay curious, stay kind and never stop asking “why.”Wishing you a Children’s Day as bright as your smile and as joyful as your laughter.Happy Children’s Day to a little star who makes every room feel happier.On this Children’s Day, may you always have big dreams, brave ideas and the courage to chase them.Today is your day! Play hard, laugh loud and enjoy that extra scoop of ice cream. Happy Children’s Day!You are loved more than you know. Wishing you the happiest Children’s Day ever.Happy Children’s Day! May your heart always stay full of wonder and your days full of fun.Keep jumping in puddles and chasing butterflies. Happy Children’s Day, little champ!Here’s to a day of cartoons, cake and endless fun. Happy Children’s Day, you deserve every bit of itDear students, may your curiosity become your strength..Messages from parents to their childrenHappy Children’s Day, my darling. You came into our lives and made everything brighter.Watching you grow is the greatest joy of our lives. Happy Children’s Day, we’re proud of you every day.Happy Children’s Day, my little one. Your hugs are the best thing about my day.I may not say it often, but you are the best part of our family. Happy Children’s Day, my child.Whatever you become, you’ll always be our little one. Happy Children’s Day, we’ll always be here for you.Thank you for teaching me patience, laughter and the joy of simple things. Happy Children’s Day, my little teacher.You make our home louder, messier and a thousand times happier. Happy Children’s Day, never change.We hope you always feel safe, heard and loved. Happy Children’s Day to our greatest gift.Your smile is our favourite sight in the world. Let’s make this Children’s Day unforgettable.No matter how tall you grow, you’ll always be our baby. Happy Children’s Day, sweetheart!Messages from teachers to studentsDear students, you fill our classrooms with energy and hope. Happy Children’s Day!Every question you ask makes me a better teacher. Happy Children’s Day, keep wondering and learning.Your potential is limitless. Happy Children’s Day, believe in yourself the way I believe in you.Happy Children’s Day! Forget homework for today and enjoy being a child. You’ve earned it.Thank you for your laughter, honesty and little surprises. Wishing every student a joyful Children’s Day.Happy Children’s Day, dear students. Mistakes are part of learning, so be brave and keep growing.You are the reason teachers love what they do. Happy Children’s Day to all my wonderful students.Dream big, work hard and be kind. That’s my Children’s Day lesson for you.Every one of you is special in your own way. Happy Children’s Day, never let anyone tell you otherwise.May your school memories stay with you long after the bell stops ringing. Happy Children’s Day!For siblings, cousins and friendsHappy Children’s Day to my favourite playmate, my partner in mischief and my best friend, little brother or sister!We may argue over the TV remote, but I’d pick you as my sibling every time. Happy Children’s Day!Remember our silly games and endless giggles? Happy Children’s Day, let’s make some more today!Happy Children’s Day to my little cousin! Wishing you a day full of treats, toys and total fun.Friends like you make childhood magical. Happy Children’s Day, buddy!Happy Children’s Day to my school friend. May we never grow out of laughing together.Here’s to secret handshakes, shared tiffins and friendships that last a lifetime. Happy Children’s Day!We’re all just kids at heart, so Happy Children’s Day to the child in you too!Thanks for being the friend I can be silly with. Have a fantastic Children’s Day!Happy Children’s Day to the little one who taught me that joy is found in the smallest things.Quotes to share“The children of today will make the India of tomorrow.” (Widely attributed to Jawaharlal Nehru, whose birthday gave Children’s Day its date.)A child’s laughter is the simplest and truest kind of happiness. Happy Children’s Day!Give a child love, time and a little freedom, and they’ll surprise you with who they become.Every child is a new beginning, full of the hope the world needs.Childhood is not a race to grow up. It’s a journey to enjoy one day at a time.Children don’t need perfect parents or perfect days. They need to feel loved and understood.“The best way to make children good is to make them happy.” (Often attributed to Oscar Wilde.)A garden of children needs sunshine, patience and plenty of room to grow.Be gentle with a child’s dreams. They are the seeds of tomorrow’s world.Protect a child’s curiosity, and you protect the future.Tips for sharing your wishesA heartfelt message doesn’t need to be long. In a card, add a personal memory, like the time your child made up a song or learned to ride a bicycle. For WhatsApp or Instagram, pair a short wish with a favourite photo and a few emojis. Teachers can read one wish aloud in class and let students write their own in return.If you can, say it in person. A hug, a bedtime story or an hour of undivided attention will mean more to a child than any message. Words are lovely, but time is what they remember.A little reminderChildren’s Day is a celebration, but it’s also a gentle nudge. Every child deserves love, safety, good food, education and room to play. Whether you’re a parent, teacher, relative or neighbour, you can play a part, even if it’s just a kind word or a donated book.Happy Children’s Day to every child out there, and to the grown-ups lucky enough to love them.Disclaimer:This article is intended for general informational and personal sharing purposes only. articles.title: Rosalía wins album of the year for ‘Lux’ at an electrifying Latin Grammy Awards
articles.summary: Spanish singer Rosalía won album of the year at the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards on Thursday night, capping an electrifying night full of stellar performances across genres.
articles.body: Spanish singer Rosalía won album of the year at the 27th annual Latin Grammy Awards on Thursday night, capping an electrifying night full of stellar performances across genres. Through tears, she started her speech in Spanish. “This is the third time I’ve won this award, and — just as ‘El Mal Querer’ felt like a dream, or ‘Motomami’ was a gamble — ‘Lux’ has been, for me, a leap into the void,” she said, referencing her 2018, 2022 and 2025 albums, respectively. “I believe it’s very important to speak your own truth and for others to be able to speak theirs; this album is my truth.” In many ways, it was the Spanish singer’s night from the very beginning. She opened the show live from Las Vegas’ MGM Grand Garden Arena, hosted by actor, producer and musician Roselyn Sánchez. Rosalía launched into an emotive medley of her “Lux” tracks “La Rumba Del Perdón,” “La Perla” and “Dios Es Un Stalker,” joined by angelic dancers ornamented with halos atop a stage meant to look like heavenly clouds. It was a reminder of the expansiveness of her album: an offbeat, full-hearted embrace of her classical training through huge orchestral movements, inspired by the lives of female saints. Some critics have argued that Rosalía, a white Catalan woman, should not be eligible for Latin Grammys, as she is from Spain and therefore not Latina. That clearly wasn’t top of mind with voters: Her “La Perla” also won song of the year. During her speech for that award, she thanked Mexico and invited her collaborators on the song, the American urban sierreño trio Yahritza Y Su Esencia, to join her on stage. A huge celebration for Daddy Yankee, too They call him the “King of Reggaeton” for a reason. Daddy Yankee, the 2026 Latin Grammy Awards’ person of the year and first Latin urbano artist to receive the honor, ripped through his biggest hits an hour into Thursday’s award show, treating the stage like a stadium floor. It was one for the history books: There were outfit changes, set changes and his native Puerto Rico always at the forefront as he ran through “Ella Me Levantó,” “Con Calma,” “BOTZ,” “Despacito,” “Lo Que Pasó, Pasó,” “Sonríele,” “Rompe,” “Pokito” and, of course, “Gasolina” — joined by Bizarrap, Bad Gyal, Feid, Jay Wheeler, French Montana, LL Cool J and Diljit Dosanjh. When it came time for Daddy Yankee to receive his honor, it was delivered to him by Janet Jackson “with admiration and respect,” as she said in her speech. When he accepted the award, he concluded by saying “Puerto Rico, recuerda. ... Puerto Rico no es pequeño. Pequeño el mapa.” In English: “Puerto Rico, remember. ... Puerto Rico is not small. The map is small.” A night of next-level performances Performances were at a high level: Karol G was joined by a full orchestra and 12 Mariachis for her música mexicana ballad “Ese Hombre es Malo.” Mon Laferte broke hearts with her soulful “Femme Fatale.” Silvana Estrada’s “Dime” bridged culture and heritage with her signature Venezuelan cuatro, a four-stringed instrument similar in structure to a ukulele. Brazilian superstar Anitta did a medley of her “Equilibrium” hits — “Desgraça,” “Choka Choka” and “Meia Noite” among them — an eclectic mix of Brazilian funk, samba, bossa nova, semba, reggae, electronic pop performed in Portuguese, Spanish and English. Soon after, she was back on stage accepting the trophy for Portuguese language contemporary pop album. She used her speech to shine a light on the Black culture of her native Brazil. There was a touching tribute to the late ranchera icon, Mexican singer-songwriter José Alfredo Jiménez, produced by Edgar Barrera: The Warning covered “Te Solté la Rienda,” Reik did “La Media Vuelta,” Sofía Reyes and Yami Safdie dueted “Si Nos Dejan” and Camila Fernández brought it home with a big belting “El Rey.” Not soon afterward, she headed back to the stage to perform a full-throated “Serpiente De Cascabel.” Barrera made history Thursday night: His career Latin Grammy wins now total 30 after Thursday night, making him the most awarded person in the show’s history. He surpassed records set by René Pérez with 29. That’s not all: On Thursday night, there was also a tribute to Willie Colón, the social activist and Grammy-nominated architect of urban salsa music, who died in February of this year. His son, Miguel Colón, as well as Nathy Peluso and Luis Figueroa and others performed. Feid also delighted, as did Kany García, who stunned with her acoustic, aflamencado single “La Niña Que Fui.” The Uruguayan-born Jorge Drexler’s rendition of “Las Palabras” felt like theater. And Argentine rapper Milo J performed “Solifican12” and “Gil,” joined by the Latin American folk icon Gustavo Santaolalla. Regional Mexican music stars Grupo Frontera launched into “Bye” and “Ojitos Bellos.” Carín León brought the house down with “Desde Que Te Tengo,” as did Juanes and Vivir Quintana with “Humano.” Elena Rose was joined by sword-wielding dancers for “Alma.” Venezuelan band Rawayana brought the party with “Bendito” and “Inglés En Miami.” A celebration of winners across genres The first award of the night was given out shortly after Rosalía’s opening set: Pablo Alboran and Backstreet Boys’ Howie D presented Juanes with best pop/rock album for “Juanesteban.” Trophies were handed out quickly from there. Milo J’s “Niño” was named record of the year. Karol G took home the trophy for urban music album for “Tropicoqueta.” Xavi won contemporary Mexican album for “Dosis,” his first Latin Grammy. His performance of “Dosis” and “No Capeã” closed the night. Fonseca was presented the trophy for contemporary tropical album shortly thereafter for his album, “Antes Que El Tiempo Se Vaya.” Best new artist went to Colombian singer Aria Vega, who gave her acceptance speech through tears. This year, the Latin Recording Academy made changes to the category so that only artists with fewer than three albums or 25 singles released were eligible to win. Most of the evening’s awards were handed out during a pre-televised Premiere Ceremony. That included Bobby Pulido winning the Latin Grammy for best Tejano album for his release “Bobby Pulido & Friends: Una Tuya y Una Mía (Vol. 2/En Vivo).” Just days earlier, Pulido made history in the U.S. midterm elections by securing a seat in the House of Representatives for the Democrats by flipping a Texas district seat. “I want to tell you that I’m retiring from music, and I’m leaving with so much gratitude,” he said in his acceptance speech.

articles.title: Russell Brand Accused Of Sexual Misconduct By Six More Women After Rape Conviction
articles.summary: Russell Brand has been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behavior by six new women after being jailed for rape and sexual assault. The Times of Lond...
articles.body:
Russell Brand has been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behavior by six new women after being jailed for rape and sexual assault.

The Times of London reported on the fresh allegations after first exposing Brand's behavior in a 2023 investigation that inspired women to report their experiences to the police. The Times ' reporting was influential in Brand being convicted last week of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

One woman has now alleged to The Times that Brand had sex with her without consent and then apologized afterwards. Another woman said Brand continued having sex with her, despite her telling the Despicable Me star that the intercourse was hurting. A third woman accused Brand of attempting to pull her into a lavatory in 2015, when the star was in a relationship with his wife, Laura Brand.

Brand, 51, has consistently denied wrongdoing and pleaded not guilty during his trial. He claimed that his behavior around women was "awful but lawful." During his trial, Brand said: "Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary, and in many ways more important than the sex itself." His lawyers did not respond to The Times ' request for comment on the fresh allegations.

One woman, identified as Alex by The Times , said Brand had sex with her without her consent when she was in her thirties. Alex was in a sexual relationship with Brand at the time, but alleged that the comedian had sex with her without a condom, despite her saying "no."

"He was very close, on top of me, and sort of pushing — but I knew he didn't have a condom on and I said, 'No, stop', and I started to sort of try and move. And … that wasn't happening," she said. Alex alleged that Brand apologized to her in person and by text message. "I justified it in my head by saying to myself: at least he admitted it," she added.

A second woman said Brand hurt her during intercourse after meeting the star in 2007 at a comedy gig. She was 19 at the time. "My body wasn't ready for this and it was painful", she said. "An uneasy wave hits me and I'm scared. And I say, 'It's painful' and he doesn't stop. And then it gets worse and it's really painful. And I say 'stop' and he doesn't stop." She added: "It was just like he … just wasn't present."

Another woman, who worked at a London venue Brand visited in 2015, said a member of his staff told her that "Russell wants you" and said: "He's in the disabled toilets". She alleged that Brand attempted to grab her when he claimed to need toilet paper.

In sentencing remarks following Brand's four-week trial, Mr Justice Bennathan described Brand as a "sexual predator." He said his fame protected him until 2023, when Channel 4 and The Times of London published allegations about his conduct.

The judge paid tribute to the "determination and bravery" of the women who made complaints about Brand. "Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say 'no' and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent," Bennathan said.

The Metropolitan Police said several people had made fresh criminal allegations about Brand during the trial. Officers are assessing the complaints.

The two have kept their relationship away from the public eye for the most part; however, they did make their relationship Instagram official earlier this year.Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau serve couple goalsDeux Moi shared photos of the two in Bereverly Hills, stepping outside of a restaurant while holding hands, dressed in their casual bests. The singer opted for an off-the-shoulder, long-sleeved black top that she chose to pair with high-waisted light-wash jeans, black heeled ankle boots, and a small black purse. She also added a pop to her fit for the night by wearing a black-and-gold belt and earrings and having her hair styled in a sleek bun. Trudeau, 54, meanwhile, went for a cozier look for the date night and opted to wear a simple blue knit sweater that he chose to pair with jeans and black shoes.The pair have reportedly been together since around July last year. The two were first spotted in Montreal on a date together, which first sparked rumors of an ongoing romance. articles.title: Sam Hartman, Washington Commanders Quarterback, Named “The” “Bachelor” for Season 30
articles.summary: The 27-year-old NFL player’s new role was announced during a Nov. 13 appearance on ABC’s ‘Good Morning America,’ just hours after the Commanders’ victory ove...
articles.body:
Sam Hartman, the 27-year-old Washington Commanders quarterback, has been named the lead of ABC's The Bachelor season 30

Sam Hartman revealed his nerves about dating 30 women during a Nov. 13 appearance on Good Morning America , where he discussed advice from Jesse Palmer and his NFL teammates

The Bachelor returns Sunday, March 21, 2027, at 8 p.m. ET/PT on ABC, with episodes streaming the next day on Hulu

Sam Hartman is trading touchdowns for roses!

The Washington Commanders quarterback, 27, has been named the next lead of ABC's The Bachelor , with the news revealed Friday, Nov. 13, during a live appearance on Good Morning America .

Hartman arrived fresh off the Commanders' Thursday night victory over the New York Giants, but admitted that finding love in front of millions of viewers might be an even more nerve-racking experience than playing professional football.

"[I'm] very nervous," he said when asked how he was feeling about the opportunity. "I have a tough time holding a conversation with one girl; 30 is gonna be pretty tough."

The NFL player revealed that his teammates had already weighed in on his upcoming reality TV adventure during their flight home.

"My teammates, they were giving me some advice on the plane ride back," he joked, before noting he couldn't repeat what they said. "Probably not going to listen to anybody on that."

Hartman also admitted that he wasn't immediately sold on the idea of becoming the franchise's newest leading man. "At first I was like, 'No way,'" he recalled. "I just think the connotation of it, I was like, 'I don't know.'"

A conversation with former Bachelor star and current franchise host Jesse Palmer, however, helped change his perspective.

"I got really lucky to talk to Jesse Palmer," Hartman explained. "He kind of gave me the insight of what it is, what it's not."

Ultimately, the chance to find a lasting relationship proved too appealing to pass up.

"I think anybody in their right mind, if you get told, 'Hey, you got a chance to go find the love of your life,'" he said. "I know one thing: When people are saying 'I do,' they don't ask you where you met, they just ask you if you want to do it forever. And I don't see any problem with that."

Hartman said his parents have also been encouraging, particularly his mother, with whom he shares a close relationship.

"They're excited. My mom and I have a really cool relationship and my pops is supportive," he said. "Their big thing is just be myself and enjoy the experience and trust your instincts, trust your gut. That's what's gotten you so far."

A native of Charlotte, N.C., Hartman made a name for himself as a standout college quarterback at Wake Forest and Notre Dame. During his college career, he set Atlantic Coast Conference records for the most career touchdown passes and 300-yard passing games.

And while The Bachelor will mark a major new chapter for the athlete, he's no stranger to reality television. Hartman previously appeared on the documentary series QB1: Beyond the Lights , which followed elite high school quarterbacks as they pursued their dreams of playing college football.

Hartman will lead the milestone 30th season of The Bachelor , which is scheduled to premiere March 21, 2027, nearly two years after the long-running dating competition last aired.

The most recent season, which concluded in March 2025, featured Grant Ellis, who proposed to Juliana Pasquarosa during the finale. The couple announced their split less than three months after the episode aired.

News of the show's return comes after a tumultuous period for the franchise, which saw the planned season of The Bachelorette starring The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives personality Taylor Frankie Paul canceled just days before its scheduled March 2026 premiere.

ABC pulled the season following the publication of footage from a 2023 domestic dispute involving Paul and her ex Dakota Mortensen , during which she was seen throwing chairs while their child was nearby .

The cancellation prompted questions about the future of the franchise, though several Bachelor Nation veterans — including Ashley Iaconetti and Trista Sutter — expressed hope that the dating competition would eventually return.

Now, with Hartman stepping into the spotlight, The Bachelor is officially preparing to hand out roses once again.

The Bachelor premieres Sunday, March 21, 2027, at 8 p.m. ET/PT on ABC, with episodes streaming the following day on Hulu.

articles.title: 'Josh' actor Sharad Kapoor fights back tears as he sends his four pet dogs to a shelter amid family and health troubles, video leaves fans worried

articles.body: Sharad Kapoor, who has shared screen space with stars such as Shah Rukh Khan and Hrithik Roshan, is in the news for a deeply emotional reason. A video of him saying goodbye to his four pet dogs has gone viral, leaving fans worried about his health and personal situation. According to animal welfare activist Hema Chaudhary, the move is only temporary, and the dogs have not been abandoned.Emotional video leaves fans worriedThe clip shows Sharad Kapoor struggling to hold back tears as his dogs are taken to an animal welfare centre. He looked visibly shaken as he bid them farewell.Many viewers remember him from films such as ‘Josh’ and were surprised to see him in this state. The actor was once talked about for his looks and fitness, but he appears quite different in the footage. Several social media users have expressed concern for him.Why did Sharad Kapoor part with his dogsAs per reports, the situation at home has made it hard for Sharad Kapoor to look after all four dogs. Hema Chaudhary said that the actor is dealing with some physical health issues and needs care himself. His family also has a newborn baby, which has added to their responsibilities.With no regular caretaker, managing four pets along with other household duties has become increasingly difficult. The family therefore decided to shift the dogs for now to YODA Mumbai, an animal welfare centre. The arrangement is expected to last until things improve and Sharad is able to look after them again.Sharad Kapoor says, 'I cannot live without them'The most touching moment in the video comes when Sharad spoke about how attached he is to his dogs. He breaks down while explaining how painful it is to be away from them.He said, “Right now, mera thoda ghar ka situation bhi hai... After this house, when I get my new bungalow, I am going to tell Yoda, Please give my babies back because I cannot live without them.”He reportedly told the centre’s representatives that he would ask for the dogs back once he has a suitable place to keep them. He described the animals as his children and said he could not imagine life without them. Sharad also worried that the dogs would be just as unhappy after being separated from him. His reaction showed just how close he is to his pets, and it is clear that this was not an easy decision for him.Activist asks people not to troll the actorHema Chaudhary, founder of the Mumbai-based Bejubaan Public Welfare Trust, shared the video online. She appealed to people not to judge or troll Sharad without knowing what he is going through. According to her, she has known the actor for almost three decades.She met him after learning about his present circumstances and understood why the family had asked for temporary help with the dogs. She made it clear that the animals were not being left behind for good. They were being moved to a shelter only because the family is finding it hard to take care of them at the moment. Her request was meant to stop needless criticism during an already difficult phase for the actor.Who is Sharad Kapoor?Sharad Kapoor has worked in several Bollywood films, but many viewers still link him with the 2000 release ‘Josh’, which starred Shah Rukh Khan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan. He played an important part in the film.His tall build, distinct look and strong screen presence helped him get noticed during his acting days. He also took up other film projects and built a place for himself in the industry over the years.Over time, however, he became less visible in mainstream entertainment and at public events. The latest video has brought him back into conversations, though for reasons far removed from cinema. While fans have reacted to his changed appearance, many have focused more on his emotional state and the tough call he had to make about his pets.The incident has also started a wider discussion on the challenges of caring for animals when a family is going through health or personal difficulties. For now, Sharad’s wish is simple: to bring his four companions back home as soon as his circumstances allow.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Standing up here alone feels wrong’: Steven Spielberg honored at Museum of Modern Art Film Benefit
articles.summary: Hollywood legend Steven Spielberg was honored at the annual event while also celebrating some of the most influential names in filmmaking.
articles.body: Hollywood legend Steven Spielberg, who at 79 remains the highest grossing director of all time, was honored on Thursday night at the Museum of Modern Art’s glitzy annual Film Benefit, an event to raise money for the institution’s film department, while also celebrating some of the most influential names in moviemaking. Spielberg’s close friends, including comedians Martin Short and Steve Martin, and industry peers such as Spike Lee and Martin Scorsese, along with beloved collaborators Drew Barrymore, Emily Blunt, and Zoe Saldaña attended to toast the director’s hugely successful five-decade career. The night even kicked off with a surprise speech from actor Tom Cruise (who starred in both Spielberg’s “Minority Report” and “War of the Worlds”). “Wow, Steven Spielberg. The very name evokes wonder, adventure, suspense, excitement, the anticipation of going to a theater and knowing that you are going to experience something extraordinary,” Cruise said. Chanel has served as the event’s head sponsor since 2011 and has been an official film partner with the museum since 2021. The french fashion house dressed a number of the evening’s VIP guests including Spielberg. Saldaña wore a sheer, jade-hued, floral embellished set with a peek-a-boo turquoise bra. Supermodel Christy Turlington was sighted in a bold black and red knit gown, and Drew Barrymore channeled the early aughts with her chunky tweed penny coat and a preppy newsboy cap. On the event’s red carpet, Spielberg recalled an early memory as a budding filmmaker. “If you look at ‘The Fablemans’ and you look at the last scene with David Lynch playing the great director John Ford, you’ll see a scene word for word, verbatim, that actually happened to me when I was in high school,” Spielberg told CNN, referencing his 2022 Oscar nominated — and semi-autobiographical — film. “When someone introduced me to John Ford and he taught me a lesson about the placement of the horizon in the frame — that’s something I never forgot.” Even those who haven’t worked with the director were quick to praise the Hollywood giant. Actor Riley Keough, a Chanel brand ambassador, said she appreciates “the way he world-builds and creates totally different universes.” “He’s an incredible filmmaker and we need incredible movies,” she added. Two musical performances helped bookmark the benefit. Ariana DeBose, who starred in Spielberg’s adaption of “West Side Story” and won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for her performance, sang a stripped down version of “Somewhere (There’s a Place for Us)” from the musical. Bruce Springsteen, who is a longtime friend of the director, closed out the evening with a rollicking rendition of “Dancing in the Dark.” In a speech on stage, Spielberg told the audience that he couldn’t have achieved all his success without the help of others. “Even though I’m the grateful and well-dressed one tonight, standing alone up here feels wrong. Filmmaking is collaborating, and when I get singled out on a night like this, it reminds me that I have never stood alone on any set, on any location, on any soundstage,” he said. “Every big production of mine has about as many people backing me up as are here tonight in this room. Imagine, please, that I am actually standing up here with every single person who ever helped me to reach this point in my career — starting with the writers, actors, and producers…making movies is making choices, and I’ve never made many choices by myself — except maybe what I eat at the craft service table. That’s about it.”

articles.body: Veteran actress Susmita Mukherjee has spoken about the toughest period of her life, when she faced money trouble and a debt of Rs 1 crore. In a recent chat, the ‘Nayyi Navelli’ actor explained how those years of emotional stress gave her the courage to speak openly and changed the way she looks at fame and money.Where her courage came fromHer honest talk about her struggles had gone viral online. She earlier revealed that she had to accept C-grade films to climb out of debt. Asked how she finds the strength to be so open, she pointed to the time she was suffering the most. She was stuck in a project that was going nowhere and was away from theatre, which she calls her first love.Speaking to NDTV, Susmita Mukherjee said, "I was going through some trauma." She added that moment made her see an artist’s role differently. She said, "Artists are supposed to be givers, not takers. We are supposed to be able to influence people."Susmita, who has grown-up sons, believes it is time to let go of worries about appearances. She said, "It is time for me to be able to express myself – not to think about how much money I have, how much time I have, what my make-up is or what my entourage is. That part should be over for people of my generation.”Susmita Mukherjee on how four hard years changed her view of moneyThe actress said the difficult phase did not make her fearful of money. It did the opposite. “Because I went through that phase – there was a phase of four years which was very bad - money has become a complete game changer for me. I look at money as energy.”She added that she now sees money as something meant to be shared, though not with any one person in particular. Her experience also taught her to trust her intentions. She said, "What I have realised now is that the universe is really malleable to your intention. It is clear to me."Faith in the toughest momentsSusmita Mukherjee recalled how she held on to hope even when her savings were nearly gone. articles.summary: Randy Travis' wife Mary reveals the emotional journey from a 1% survival chance to releasing "Same Old Way" more than a decade after his stroke.
articles.body: Randy Travis' life was turned upside down by a devastating health crisis that doctors gave him just a 1% chance of surviving, according to his wife, Mary. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, the country legend — whose new 12-track album, "Same Old Way," is out now — and his wife, Mary, reflected on that life-changing ordeal more than a decade ago, explained how hope and faith played a pivotal role in his recovery, and shared how his determination helped him rebuild his life and reconnect with music. "They had already told us he had 1% chance of survival. And that was the first couple of days in the hospital," Mary said. "So here we are, five and a half months later, he's still here. He's still improving. We went through the second brain surgery. He came through that with flying colors. The first one is when they said he's not, you know, he doesn't have any chance. But, you know, once you get over those and you start seeing the glimmers of hope and the hand of God on the whole thing." RANDY TRAVIS' HEALTH CRISIS BEGAN WITH 'CONGESTION' AND ENDED IN A FIVE-MONTH HOSPITAL STAY The "Forever and Ever, Amen" singer was hospitalized in 2013 for congestive heart failure tied to viral cardiomyopathy. He subsequently suffered a massive stroke that left him with partial paralysis and affected his speech. What began as a trip to seek treatment for congestion became a five-and-a-half-month hospital stay, followed by years of rehabilitation. "We went through three years of rehab every single day, so we were very quiet and out of the limelight, if you will," she added. "We, you know, we were at home. We went to rehab every day for about three years." Eventually, Mary said, Travis "got tired" of the constant rehabilitation and decided to "go live life." Their trips back to Nashville helped renew their hope that he could once again be involved in the music he loved. WATCH: RANDY TRAVIS’ WIFE SAYS DOCTORS GAVE COUNTRY LEGEND 1% CHANCE OF SURVIVAL BEFORE MIRACULOUS COMEBACK Travis has since found new ways to share his music and connect with fans. In May 2024, he released "Where That Came From," using AI technology to recreate his signature singing voice. His "More Life" tour continued through 2026, with Travis appearing alongside Mary while guest vocalist James Dupré and his longtime band perform his hits. VINCE GILL GAVE AMY GRANT A REALITY CHECK DURING RECOVERY FROM BRAIN INJURY Now, with the release of his first album of original material in more than 18 years — featuring 12 previously unreleased songs recorded between 1986 and 2013 and restored by his longtime producer, Kyle Lehning — Mary is reflecting on the determination and gratitude that carried her husband through his toughest moments. CELINE DION BREAKS DOWN ONSTAGE DURING EMOTIONAL RETURN AFTER 6-YEAR HIATUS "Just being with this guy has been such an inspiration to me because, going through even the tough times in the hospital, the nurses would come in and cut him or stick him or poke him or do whatever, and they'd walk out the door. And if he wasn't in his coma and he was aware, he’d say, ‘Thank you.’ That was Randy Travis," she said. "And they'd turn around and look like, you got to be kidding me, you know. But that was Randy Travis." That same spirit, she said, followed him into rehabilitation and remains evident today, even as aphasia continues to affect his ability to communicate. "I have pictures of him there in the rehab center and he's smiling. He's laughing. He’s giving it all he's got. Randy Travis hasn't changed. And that's still the man that I get to sit beside right now," she said. "He still has that, that love for life, the love for people." For Mary, the release of "Same Old Way" is especially emotional because it represents an opportunity they once weren't sure would ever come again. Before his stroke, she said, they assumed there would be many more albums and years of making music ahead. BILLY RAY CYRUS CHEATED DEATH DURING SEPSIS, VOCAL PARALYSIS BATTLE BEFORE STAGING MUSIC COMEBACK "It's really an emotional thing, because 18 years ago when he put out his last one, we thought that the world was an oyster and there was gonna be so many more," she said. "But the stroke happened, it was 13 years ago, and everything changed." "Thirteen years ago, we had no idea, based on where we were then, when we were in the hospital, that we would have this opportunity. So, in a way, it’s a miracle," she added. "I get emotional when I think about it, just because I wanted to hear his voice so bad again." Hearing those recordings, Mary explained, offers listeners a chance to experience Travis' voice at different stages of his life — and gives the couple another reason to appreciate how far he has come. articles.title: Viral firing video helps city police bust gun-running racket
articles.summary: Viral blank-firing video leads Bhubaneswar police to bust illegal arms racket; man arrested with two pistols, 8 bullets; links probed to Bihar’s Munger.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: A viral video of a man resorting to blank firing at a festival in Bhubaneswar has helped the special crime unit (SCU) of the commissionerate police bust an illegal firearms trading racket. The SCU arrested the man on Friday and seized two illegal semi-automatic pistols and eight rounds of ammunition from his possession, suspecting his link with interstate arms dealers. The accused was identified as Biswajit Behera (33) of Gobindpur in Cuttack district.“After coming across the viral video, we kept him under surveillance. Acting on a tip-off, we intercepted Behera’s vehicle near the block office in Balipatna on the city’s outskirts. A search led to the recovery of the two firearms and eight bullets,” said DCP (SCU) Anup Kumar Kanungo.During interrogation, Behera allegedly told police that he had purchased the weapons from a Bhubaneswar-based supplier, who sourced them from Munger in Bihar, a major hub for illegal firearms manufacturing. He claimed he procured the weapons for self-protection, fearing attacks by anti-social elements because of his sand mining business.“We are probing the supply chain, financial transactions involved in the purchase and possible links of the accused with other criminal networks. Behera was previously booked in five cases involving criminal intimidation and assault at Olatpur and Gobindpur police stations in Cuttack district over the past year,” Kanungo said.The seizure comes amid growing concerns over the use of illegal firearms in Bhubaneswar, with three firing incidents reported in the past three months. On Nov 7, a youth was shot dead at point-blank range in Laxmisagar, allegedly over gang rivalry. Two days earlier, a man died after being accidentally shot with an illegal firearm during celebratory firing in the Sisupalgarh area.
